waiverExpiryFields.fieldDesign: Add TWO optional fields to the Waiver interface at scripts/upstream-sync-record.ts:61-66 (currently {path:62, direction:63, decision:65, ticket:66}, no expiry). (1) expiresOn?: string — an ISO-8601 instant (reuse the existing ISO_INSTANT regex at :24 for validation), a CALENDAR expiry. (2) expiresAfterSyncs?: number — a positive integer, a SYNC-COUNT fuse = max recorded syncs the waiver may survive while still matching before promoting. DELIBERATELY do NOT add a recordedAtSync creation-anchor field in the first cut: expiresAfterSyncs anchors against the total recorded sync count (record.history.length + 1), which is crude if a waiver is added to a record that already has history, but the record grows one sync at a time so this is fine for the common case. Flag recordedAtSync as a future refinement only if the crude anchor bites. Do NOT add both fields mandatorily — keep allows permanent keep (current behavior) when neither is set; expiry is opt-in per waiver. Known-red expiry (the §2 meta-gate half) is a SEPARATE field design on a SEPARATE interface — see knownRedExpiry.
waiverExpiryFields.semantics: Three decision types (WaiverDecision at :55 = 'pending'|'keep'|'drop'), each with distinct expiry semantics. KEEP (permanent acceptance): if expiresOn/expiresAfterSyncs set and tripped while the waiver STILL MATCHES a finding -> FAILURE (keep-decision is stale, re-adjudicate); the point of expiry here is to force periodic re-review of permanent divergences. If a keep waiver matches 0 findings AND its fuse is tripped -> FAILURE (stale waiver, re-adjudicate or remove); if 0 hits and no fuse -> NOTE (existing behavior, unchanged). DROP (remediation owed via ticket): carries a HARD expiry — expiresAfterSyncs or expiresOn tied to the ticket's expected resolution; if the fuse trips while the waiver still matches -> FAILURE ('debt past deadline', escalation so remediation cannot be parked forever). The ticket field (:66) already exists to name the owing ticket; the gate does NOT resolve ticket state (wayfinder .md files are not git-resolvable), so the expiry date is human-set at adjudication time. PENDING (not-yet-decided): SHORTEST FUSE — a pending waiver that still matches a finding is a FAILURE unconditionally (live undecided divergence), and if no explicit expiresAfterSyncs is set, defaults to expiresAfterSyncs:1 (must not survive >1 sync round). NOTE: the current upstream-sync.json has 0 pending waivers (commit 2d4da9b468 flipped the ui-settings-models umbrella from pending->keep), so the pending-fuse has nothing to calibrate against today but must be in the schema for future syncs.
waiverExpiryFields.collectGitFailuresChange: The promotion site is the zero-hit note loop at scripts/upstream-sync-record.ts:207-217 (the `for (const [index, waiver]...` block with `report.notes.push('waiver ... matched no finding ... stale')`). Today this loop is decision-inert AND expiry-inert: it emits a NOTE iff matched===0, and never consults waiver.decision. Replace it with expiry-aware branching: compute recordedSyncCount=record.history.length+1, now, expired=(expiresOn!==undefined && Date.parse(expiresOn)<=now), syncFuseTripped=(expiresAfterSyncs!==undefined && recordedSyncCount>=expiresAfterSyncs). Then: (a) decision:'pending' + matched>0 -> FAILURE (live undecided); (b) matched===0 + (syncFuseTripped||expired) -> FAILURE ('matched no finding across N sync(s) and expired — re-adjudicate or remove'); (c) matched===0 + no fuse -> NOTE (existing, preserved); (d) matched>0 + expired -> FAILURE ('expired but still matches — re-adjudicate'); (e) decision:'drop' + matched>0 + syncFuseTripped -> FAILURE ('drop survived N sync(s) past fuse with remediation owed via {ticket} — debt past deadline'); (f) decision:'keep' + matched>0 + not expired -> suppressed (existing, waiver works as intended). CRITICAL design choice: an expired waiver should also RE-SURFACE the underlying finding failures it suppressed, so that adjudicate (:762-778) must be extended to track suppressed findings per waiver index (hits:Map<number,number> -> also suppressed:Map<number,IntegrityFinding[]>, recording each finding at the hits.set call at :777). The post-loop then pushes those suppressed findings as failures for expired waivers. matchWaiver (:746) STAYS decision-inert and expiry-inert — matching is purely structural (direction+path); decision/expiry enforcement lives ONLY in the post-adjudication loop. This is an intentional clean separation: matching answers 'does this divergence have a waiver'; the post-loop answers 'is that waiver still valid'.

knownRedExpiry.design: Known-red expiry is a SEPARATE policy on a SEPARATE interface (gate-coverage.manifest.json + verify-gate-coverage.ts), NOT on the Waiver interface. Design (for when §2 lands): each knownRed entry carries (1) reopenTrigger — a SEMANTIC, human-readable string (e.g. 'product internationalization' for verify-client-ui-i18n, 'fork README skeleton retrofit complete' for doc-standard-tests) that documents WHEN to revisit but is NOT machine-checkable; (2) reviewBy?: string — an ISO-8601 DATE that IS machine-checkable. In verify-gate-coverage.ts, add Check 5 (after the §2 Check 4 that asserts every knownRed names an enrolled gate): a knownRed entry past its reviewBy date flips from silently-accepted to must-re-justify — the meta-gate emits a FAILURE ('known-red {script} past review-by {date}; re-justify, remove, or extend'). reopenTrigger is documentation; reviewBy is the expiry. Default reviewBy (e.g. +90 or +180 days from enrollment) is a calibration question. This is the structural cure for the orphan pattern UM-C-GATES fixed reactively (C-class 4 gates orphaned 2026-09-07->2026-09-11): a known-red with no reviewBy should itself be a meta-gate failure (every known-red must carry an explicit review-by date, not be open-ended).
knownRedExpiry.blockedOn: BLOCKED on the §2 knownRed[] schema extension, which does not exist yet. CONFIRMED by reading verify-gate-coverage.ts: it has Check 1 (enrolled-OR-exempted), Check 2 (exemption references existing script), Check 3 (no exemption for now-enrolled script) — and NOTHING else. There is no knownRed[] array, no Check 4, no upstream-sync.json cross-reference. The manifest interface is GateCoverageManifest={exemptions:[{script,reason,coveredBy}]} only (gate-coverage.manifest.json: 20 exemptions, no knownRed). So 'known-red expiry has nothing to expire' — the §2 knownRed[] + Check 4 prerequisite must land FIRST. NEW FILE scripts/upstream-sync-record.spec.ts — there is NO dedicated spec today (confirmed: find returned only the .ts itself; run-gates.spec.ts references upstream-sync only for gate-wiring). Model the new spec on scripts/verify-gate-coverage.spec.ts:1-40 (scaffold() tmp-dir pattern with mkdtempSync). Required cases: (a) keep+notExpired+matches->pass; (b) keep+expired+matches->FAILURE; (c) drop+syncFuseTripped+matches->FAILURE; (d) pending+matches->FAILURE; (e) zeroHit+fuseTripped->FAILURE; (f) zeroHit+noFuse->NOTE (regression-guard the existing behavior); (g) shape validation rejects non-ISO expiresOn and non-positive expiresAfterSyncs; (h) rejects expiresOn+expiresAfterSyncs both set.
calibrationQuestions: N-syncs default for expiresAfterSyncs by decision: for KEEP (periodic re-review of permanent divergences) — 3 or 4 syncs? For DROP (debt escalation) — should it default to the owing ticket's SLA, or a fixed 2-sync fuse? For PENDING — confirm the 1-sync default (must not survive a round). These are human judgment in the same family as the cadence thresholds (150 commits / 14 days).

Calendar expiry windows: should expiresOn have a default (e.g. +90 or +180 days from recording) when a human adjudicates, or must it always be explicitly set? And should KEEP waivers be ALLOWED to set NO expiry (permanent keep = current behavior), or should every keep carry a mandatory review-by (no open-ended permanent keeps)?

Re-surface scope: when a waiver expires, should the gate re-surface the underlying suppressed findings as failures (my design, more noise but forces the divergence to show), or emit only a waiver-level failure (cheaper, less noisy, but the finding stays hidden behind an expired waiver)? This determines whether the suppressed Map is needed.

The crude anchor: expiresAfterSyncs counts against total recorded syncs (history.length+1), not 'syncs since the waiver was created'. If a waiver is added to a record that already has 3 syncs in history, a fuse of 2 trips immediately. Is this acceptable for the first cut, or must recordedAtSync (creation anchor) ship from day one? Note: the current record has only 1 history + 1 current = 2 syncs, so it's not urgent.

Should decision:'pending' waivers auto-fail when they survive >1 sync WITHOUT an explicit expiresAfterSyncs (default=1), or only fail if a human explicitly set a fuse? I.e., is the shortest-fuse a hard default or opt-in?

Known-red reviewBy default (for the §2 half, once unblocked): +90 days, +180 days, or tied to a fiscal/quarter cadence? And should a knownRed entry with NO reviewBy be a meta-gate failure (every known-red must have an explicit review date)?
